title: Bump the pinned bun 1.3.14 to >=1.4.0 (1.3.14 silently strips a top-level binding named declare)
description:
Fleet notice OPAG-734 (opum-agent, 2026-09-29, corrected same day): bun 1.3.14 silently strips a top-level binding named "declare" in a .ts file. `function declare(v) {...}; declare('x')` prints nothing and exits 0, and so does a const/let/var form -- a member call `obj.declare()` runs normally. A test helper named declare would therefore not execute while its assertions passed vacuously. Upstream oven-sh/bun#30006, fixed by oven-sh/bun#31239, which is in bun 1.4.0 and later but not 1.3.14.

This repository pins bun@1.3.14 in package.json's packageManager and in every oven-sh/setup-bun step across .github/workflows/ (projection-platform.yml, lore-check.yml, prepublication-qualification.yml -- four steps).

NOT URGENT, measured rather than assumed: 0 occurrences of the pattern in 192 tracked .ts files on dev 0c49b792, working tree and origin/dev by ref agreeing at 192 (git ls-tree -r origin/dev --name-only, counting .ts). Run with the corrected pattern and a positive control in the same invocation: it fires on `function declare` and `export const declare` and not on `obj.declare()` or `declared`. The exposure is future code, not present code.

Scheduling: OPAG-734 notes lore and quest release as a pair, so this rides a release rather than needing one of its own. Check that packageManager and the CI pins move together, and whether any other fleet tooling reads this repository's pin.

acceptanceCriteria.text: package.json packageManager and every bun-version pin in .github/workflows/ name a bun at 1.4.0 or later, and CI is green on the pinned version
A check runs the OPAG-734 repro at the pinned version and proves the binding executes (output present, exit 0) rather than being stripped silently, so a future downgrade is caught

plan: 1. Move packageManager and every CI bun-version pin to 1.4.2, and @types/bun with them; regenerate the lockfile with the pinned runtime so CI frozen-lockfile install matches.
2. Prove the OPAG-734 repro flips: silent on 1.3.14, printing on 1.4.2 (measured, both binaries in hand).
3. Add a check that runs the repro at the pinned version via process.execPath and fails loudly, naming the running bun version, when the binding is stripped.
4. Gates with the pinned runtime first on PATH: bun run check and lore check.
5. Deliver per opum-sdlc on dev. NO release: Article 3 pairs lore and quest, and lore-cli still pins 1.3.14, so the carrying release is a pair decision for later.
implementationNotes:
ACs 1-2 evidence. Both halves of the OPAG-734 repro were MEASURED, not taken from the notice: at 1.3.14 the program prints only "after the call" and exits 0, with the "declare printed: x" line absent; at 1.4.2 it prints both, exit 0. The 1.4.2 binary was fetched to scratch (/tmp/qcli411-bun, darwin-arm64, from the official release) rather than upgrading the machine's bun, which other repos on this machine are pinned against.

AC1: packageManager, @types/bun and every CI bun-version pin now name 1.4.2. THE DESCRIPTION'S ENUMERATION WAS INCOMPLETE, which is why the static half discovers workflows instead of listing them: it says four steps across projection-platform.yml, lore-check.yml and prepublication-qualification.yml, but there are FIVE, because tracker-integrity.yml carries one too. bun.lock was regenerated with 1.4.2 itself (bun install under the pinned runtime), so CI's frozen-lockfile install compares against a lockfile written by the runtime the pin names -- the runbook's own instruction, "check bun --version against package.json's packageManager before touching bun.lock", followed rather than paraphrased. Evidence: bun run check under the pinned runtime, 1005 pass / 0 fail (was 1003/113 files; the two new tests and one new file account for the delta); check:lockfile exit 0, "bun.lock pins all 6 of 6 platform packages"; lore check exit 0, 63 files, 0 errors.

AC2: test/qcli411-bun-declare-binding.test.ts, two tests. The static half asserts every bun pin is >= 1.4.0, discovering .github/workflows rather than listing it, so a new workflow with a stale pin is caught and a partial revert fails. The runtime half writes the repro to a temp dir and runs it through process.execPath -- the runtime actually running the suite, so under CI that is the pinned one -- and fails if the call did not execute, naming OPAG-734 and the remedy.

TWO-SIDED CONTROL, and the prediction was that exactly one test would move: on 1.4.2 both pass; on 1.3.14 the runtime half fails with the binding-stripped message while the static half passes. That split is what distinguishes this from a pin edit dressed as a check: the pins were already 1.4.2 in both runs, so nothing but the runtime changed between them.

FOUND WHILE MEASURING, and worth more than the bump itself: Bun.Glob changed between the two versions. `.github/workflows/*` returns 0 files on 1.3.14 and 7 on 1.4.2, unless `dot: true` is passed, which returns 7 on both. So the natural way to write the static half reads NOTHING on exactly the runtime it exists to complain about -- and its read-nothing guard, not its version assertion, is what fires. That is how it surfaced: the 1.3.14 control initially failed the static test at the guard line. The test now passes dot: true with a comment saying why, and filters the extension in JS rather than with a brace glob for the same reason.

FLEET TOOLING QUESTION (the task asked whether any other tooling reads this pin): nothing does, live. Searching opum-agent, opum-cli-e2e, lore-cli, opum-doc, opum-fleet, quest-web and lore-web for "1.3.14" turns up only (a) frozen replay fixtures in opum-agent/tooling/fleet-sweep/test/fixtures/paths-coverage/, which record quest-cli's package.json AT A NAMED REF and must not be edited -- changing them would falsify the fixture the audit replays; (b) dated records, ADRs and runbook measurements that name the version as measured history, which rewriting would falsify per the retirement-scope rule; and (c) lore-cli's own pin, which is lore-cli's business and is why no release is cut here. Nothing reads the value programmatically.

NOT DONE, deliberately, and named so the release does not inherit it silently: the committed npm/* platform binaries remain 1.3.14-built. On a tag ref the workflow executes the COMMITTED artifact rather than rebuilding it (QCLI-135: a rebuild is a different artifact from the one attested), so the next release's own rebuild-and-commit step is what carries the new pin into the shipped binaries. That step already exists in the release runbook; this task does not cut a release, so it does not pre-empt it.

PROMOTION HOLD, ruled by opum-agent 2026-09-29. dev is deliberately ONE COMMIT AHEAD of main — a712ebdf over 5b8faf89, and that one commit is this task's bun pin. DO NOT PROMOTE quest-cli's dev to main until opum-agent says the pair is ready.

WHY, in the ruling's own terms: Article 3 pairs the lore and quest runtimes, lore-cli still pins bun 1.3.14, and LCLI-648 is the matching bump on lore-cli's own dev. The two repositories promote TOGETHER once LCLI-648 has landed there, so neither main carries half of a paired runtime change. Promoting quest-cli alone would put a 1.4.2 pin on the ref releases are cut from while its pair is still on 1.3.14 — which is the outcome "cut NO release" on this task already existed to prevent, one step earlier.

NOT A STANDING HOLD. The ruling is explicit that it is an execution ruling for this task only, and says so in those words: "This is an execution ruling for this task only. It is not a standing hold on quest-cli promotions." A successor must not generalise it into a policy that outlives the pair, and must not read it as precedent for holding an unrelated promotion later.

WHAT UNBLOCKS IT: opum-agent telling this repository that LCLI-648 has landed on lore-cli's dev. The successor does not verify lore-cli itself and does not promote on its own initiative even if it observes lore-cli looking ready — the orchestrator names the moment. If a successor finds itself wanting to promote for any other reason, that is a question for opum-agent, not a judgement call.

The rest of the batch is already released: QCLI-377 and QCLI-412 are on main at 5b8faf89. Only this commit is held.

SESSION HANDOFF, written at the orchestrator's recycle request (2026-09-29, opum-agent recycling this session for context budget). This note is the handoff artifact and is written AFTER the recycle request, so it is the one to restore from. Everything below was measured or ruled, not inferred unless it says so.

RESUME POINT AND REPOSITORY STATE: dev checked out level with origin/dev at the close of this session, clean tree, no open PRs from it. main = 5b8faf89 (QCLI-377 and QCLI-412 released). At the moment this note was written, dev was deliberately ONE COMMIT AHEAD of main: a712ebdf, which is this task's bun pin. See the hold note below before touching that.

1. PROMOTION HOLD - DO NOT PROMOTE quest-cli's dev to main until opum-agent says the pair is ready. Reason: Article 3 pairs the lore and quest runtimes, lore-cli still pins bun 1.3.14, and LCLI-648 is the matching bump on lore-cli's own dev. The two repositories promote TOGETHER once LCLI-648 has landed there, so neither main carries half of a paired runtime change. A successor does NOT verify lore-cli itself and does NOT promote even if lore-cli looks ready - the orchestrator names the moment. opum-agent's ruling is explicit that this is an execution ruling for this task only and NOT a standing hold on quest-cli promotions; do not generalise it into a policy that outlives the pair. The full reasoning is in the previous note on this record.

2. THE BUN TRAP - the single most likely thing to waste a successor's first hour. dev pins bun 1.4.2 (this task's change) while the MACHINE runs 1.3.14. A plain `bun run check` therefore FAILS at test/qcli411-bun-declare-binding.test.ts with "bun 1.3.14 silently stripped a top-level binding named `declare`". That red is the check WORKING, not a regression. Remedy, run the suite on the pinned runtime rather than downgrading the pin or ignoring the failure:

    curl -sSL -o /tmp/bun.zip "https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.4.2/bun-darwin-aarch64.zip"
    unzip -oq /tmp/bun.zip -d /tmp/qcli411-bun
    PATH=/tmp/qcli411-bun/bun-darwin-aarch64:$PATH bun run check

The PATH prefix is load-bearing: `bun run check` is a chain of nested `bun run` calls that each re-resolve bun from PATH, so without it the chain mixes two runtimes. opum-agent is passing the same remedy to lore-cli for LCLI-648.

3. REMAINING ITEMS, none of them this session's to start:
- QCLI-413 (the staging hint does not reach --json callers; a contract change) WAITS ON DEC-21. I sent the operator A/B packet through opum-agent, who filed it as DEC-21 with my premise caveat carried as the lead. DO NOT start, branch or land QCLI-413 until DEC-21 is answered. Worth keeping: my attempt to measure the premise ("most fleet sessions call quest with --json") was CONTAMINATED - a grep over 82 transcript files matched prose (help text, task descriptions, changelogs), not command lines - so the packet states the premise as unverified rather than resting on that number. Unflagged invocations are auto-selected to --plain off a TTY and DO see the human-surface hint, so part of the premise is probably wrong.
- QCLI-406 (move Closed into terminalStatuses) - trigger has NOT fired; it waits on a tolerant lore being the floor.
- QCLI-399 (publish the root launcher's final X straight to latest) - Paused.

4. WHAT LANDED THIS SESSION, so a successor does not redo it: QCLI-377 (README.md and LICENSE added to the source-gates push paths) and QCLI-412 (the staging hint extended to close, archive and demote) are released on main at 5b8faf89. QCLI-411 (bun 1.4.2 pin plus a runtime check for the declare binding) is on dev and held from promotion by item 1. A ward-cli finding about `task list --status Paused` was reproduced, found to be a duplicate of QCLI-392 (fixed on dev, absent from released v0.11.0 - one version string naming two byte-sets), and DECLINED with that reason rather than filed.

5. SKILLS THE NEXT SESSION SHOULD REACH FOR: opum-sdlc for the branch-PR-land path (its no-exemption rule applies to tracker-only changes like this one); opum-handoff for restore; opum-quest for tracker writes. Scope the merge decision by reading the required contexts from the ruleset and intersecting by name - do NOT use mergeStateStatus, which never reaches CLEAN on a promotion PR here, and do NOT count rows, because a .quest-only head legitimately produces ONE source-gates row and a source-touching head produces TWO.
finalSummary:
The bun pin moves to 1.4.2 and a check now holds the pin to the behaviour that motivated it. Bun 1.3.14 silently STRIPS a top-level binding named `declare` in a .ts file -- `function declare(v) {...}; declare('x')` prints nothing and exits 0 -- so a test helper of that name would never run while the assertions around it passed vacuously. Upstream oven-sh/bun#30006, fixed by oven-sh/bun#31239, in 1.4.0 and later but not 1.3.14 (OPAG-734).

WHAT MOVED: package.json packageManager and @types/bun, and all FIVE oven-sh/setup-bun steps across four workflows. The task description enumerated four steps across three workflows and missed tracker-integrity.yml, which is why the new static check discovers workflows rather than listing them. bun.lock was regenerated WITH 1.4.2 itself, so CI's frozen-lockfile install compares against a lockfile written by the runtime the pin names -- the runbook's own instruction, followed rather than paraphrased.

VERIFIED, and measured rather than inferred:
- Both halves of the repro, in hand: at 1.3.14 the program prints only "after the call"; at 1.4.2 it prints "declare printed: x" then "after the call". Both exit 0. The 1.4.2 binary was fetched to scratch rather than upgrading the machine's bun, which other repos on this machine pin against.
- AC1: CI green on the pinned version, and CONFIRMED to be running it rather than merely green -- the source-gates job log shows setup-bun downloading bun-v1.4.2, `bun install --frozen-lockfile --linker=isolated` reporting `bun install v1.4.2` and `+ @types/bun@1.4.2`, and the resolved test list containing qcli411-bun-declare-binding.test.ts. Locally the full suite ran under the pinned runtime: 1005 pass, 0 fail (1003 before; the delta is the two new tests and one new file). check:lockfile exit 0, lore check exit 0.
- AC2: test/qcli411-bun-declare-binding.test.ts. Static half asserts every pin is >= 1.4.0, workflows discovered, so a partial revert or a new workflow with a stale pin fails. Runtime half runs the repro through process.execPath -- the runtime actually running the suite -- and fails naming OPAG-734 and the remedy. Two-sided control: 2 pass on 1.4.2; on 1.3.14 the runtime half fails with the binding-stripped message while the static half passes. The pins were identical in both runs, so only the runtime changed between them.

FOUND WHILE MEASURING, worth more than the bump: Bun.Glob changed between the two versions. `.github/workflows/*` returns 0 files on 1.3.14 and 7 on 1.4.2 unless `dot: true` is passed, which returns 7 on both. The natural way to write the static half therefore reads NOTHING on exactly the runtime it exists to complain about, and its read-nothing guard fires instead of its version assertion -- which is how the 1.3.14 control failed on the first run. The test now passes dot: true with the reason recorded.

FLEET TOOLING: nothing reads this pin live. Searching the seven sibling repos turns up only frozen replay fixtures in opum-agent's paths-coverage test data (which record quest-cli's package.json at a NAMED REF and must not be edited), dated records and runbook measurements that name the version as measured history, and lore-cli's own independent pin -- which is why no release is cut here (Article 3 pairs lore and quest).

NOT DONE, named so the release does not inherit it silently: the committed npm/* platform binaries remain 1.3.14-built. On a tag ref the workflow executes the COMMITTED artifact rather than rebuilding it (QCLI-135), so the release's own rebuild-and-commit step is what carries the new pin into the shipped binaries. That step already exists in the runbook; this task does not cut a release and does not pre-empt it.
